title: EMS Handoff Summary
author: K. Ruiz, Paramedic (Medic 4)
summary: 34 M, house fire victim with flame burns and smoke inhalation, 500 mL LR and high-flow O2 given en route, handed off to ED at 02:30.
body:
**Dispatch and Times**
- Call received 01:38 for structure fire with reported injured occupant. Medic 4 on scene 01:55, patient contact 02:00, left scene 02:14, arrived ED 02:30. Transfer of care to A. Torres, RN and Dr. Castellano at 02:30.

**Scene and Mechanism**
- Single-family house fire, estimated time of injury 01:30. Patient is a 34-year-old male who per his partner fell asleep on the couch after drinking alcohol and smoking, woke to heavy smoke, and went back into the enclosed, smoke-filled house to carry his 6-year-old daughter out. He was found by firefighters on the front lawn outside the structure, coughing and sitting upright. Partner (Jenna Whitaker) and daughter (Ava) were outside and uninjured; a second unit evaluated them and transported them to the ED for observation.
- Flame burns to right arm and anterior chest. Prolonged exposure to smoke in an enclosed space. No fall, no blunt trauma, no loss of consciousness per witnesses. Spinal motion restriction not indicated.

**Primary Assessment**
- Airway: hoarse voice, soot around nares and mouth, singed nasal hairs, productive cough with black sputum. No stridor at scene contact; mild inspiratory noise noted en route.
- Breathing: tachypneic, bilateral wheezes and scattered rhonchi. Circulation: radial pulses present left, weak right hand. Disability: GCS 15, alert and oriented, smells of alcohol, anxious. Exposure: burns as below.

**Vital Signs**
- 02:03: HR 126, BP 142/86, RR 26, SpO2 94% room air. After NRB 15 L/min: SpO2 99%.
- 02:25: HR 120, BP 136/82, RR 24, SpO2 99% on NRB. Glucose 138 mg/dL. Cardiac monitor sinus tachycardia, no ectopy. Temp not obtained.

**Burn Assessment**
- Estimated 20% TBSA by rule of nines: right arm circumferential (approx 9%), anterior chest (approx 9%), face and neck. Right forearm and hand appear leathery and white; right hand swollen. Pain 8/10.

**Treatment**
- 100% O2 by non-rebreather mask 15 L/min from 02:03 (carbon monoxide exposure suspected).
- IV 20 g left hand. Lactated Ringer's 500 mL infused en route (documented 02:20).
- Burned areas covered with dry sterile burn sheets; no creams or wet dressings applied. Jewelry removed from right hand. Kept warm with blankets.
- No analgesics given prehospital (short transport, airway concern).

**Handoff**
- Report given to ED: concern for inhalation injury and impending airway compromise; patient alert and protecting airway at handoff. Belongings given to partner.

title: ED Provider Note
author: M. Castellano, MD
summary: ED course for a 34 M with 22% TBSA flame burns and inhalation injury: intubated 02:50, escharotomy 03:15, resuscitation started, admitted to Burn ICU.
body:
**Chief Complaint**
Burns to right arm, chest and face after house fire; smoke inhalation.

**HPI**
34-year-old male, arrived by EMS 02:30 after a house fire (injury about 01:30). He fell asleep on the couch after drinking and smoking, woke to smoke and re-entered to carry his 6-year-old daughter out; found outside by firefighters. Received O2 by NRB and LR 500 mL from EMS. PMH childhood asthma (resolved), seasonal allergies. Meds: cetirizine PRN. NKDA. Tobacco 1 ppd x 15 years, alcohol on weekends, no drugs. Tdap unknown, more than 10 years ago.

**Primary Survey (02:30-02:35)**
- A: hoarse voice, soot in oropharynx and nares, singed nasal hair, facial burns, early inspiratory stridor developing. B: RR 24, wheezes and rhonchi, SpO2 99% on NRB (unreliable with CO exposure). C: HR 118, BP 138/84 (MAP 102), cap refill about 3 sec right hand. D: GCS 15. E: temp 96.8 F, warmed.

**Secondary Survey**
- Right arm circumferential burn, forearm and hand leathery full thickness, upper arm deep partial; anterior chest deep partial with full-thickness patches; face and neck superficial to partial. Bilateral corneas clear with fluorescein. TBSA 22% (confirmed with Dr. Okafor), about 8% full thickness. No other injuries.

**Airway Decision**
Hoarseness, developing stridor, singed nasal hair, soot and facial burns indicate high risk for rapid upper airway edema. Decision for early definitive airway. RSI at 02:50 with etomidate 20 mg and rocuronium 100 mg; 8.0 ETT placed, 24 cm at the teeth, direct laryngoscopy, grade 2 view with edema (see procedure note). Placed on AC/VC 450/16, PEEP 5, FiO2 1.0. Post-intubation HR 116, BP 116/72 at 03:05.

**Studies**
- 02:40 labs: WBC 12.8, Hgb 17.2, Plt 288, Na 138, K 4.3, CO2 19, Cr 0.9, glucose 143, lactate 5.8 (02:50), ethanol 42 mg/dL, INR 1.1, troponin I 0.02, CK 480. UDS negative. UA dark amber, SG 1.031, myoglobin negative.
- ABG 02:50 (on 100% O2): pH 7.29, PaCO2 38, PaO2 412, HCO3 18, BE -7, COHb 14.2%. Pulse oximeter overestimates saturation in CO poisoning.
- Cyanide considered given lactate 5.8 and soot exposure; patient hemodynamically stable with intact mentation, so hydroxocobalamin not given; lactate to be rechecked after fluids.

**Resuscitation**
- Parkland: 4 mL x 82 kg x 22% = 7,216 mL LR in 24 h from injury (01:30). Half (3,608 mL) in the first 8 h (to 09:30), remainder over the next 16 h. EMS 500 mL counted; remaining 3,108 mL over 7 h is about 444 mL/h. LR started 02:30 at 450 mL/h, titrate to UOP 30-50 mL/h (0.5 mL/kg/h).
- Left AC 18 g PIV 02:40. Foley 02:45 (dark amber urine). OG tube 16 Fr 03:05. Left IJ triple-lumen CVC placed 03:45 under ultrasound (see procedure note).

**Medications**
- Fentanyl 100 mcg IV 02:36, infusion 50 mcg/h from 03:00, bolus 100 mcg at 03:12, infusion increased to 100 mcg/h at 03:40. Propofol started 02:55. Albuterol 2.5 mg neb 02:45. Tdap 0.5 mL IM 03:30.

**Burn Surgery**
Dr. Okafor called 02:55, at bedside 03:10. Right forearm tense with absent Doppler signals to the hand and pain: bedside escharotomy at 03:15 with return of Doppler signals (see his note). Chest ventilation adequate, PIP 28, escharotomy not needed.

**Imaging**
Portable CXR 03:20: ETT 4 cm above carina, OG in stomach, lungs clear to mild perihilar haze.

**Vitals at 03:55**
HR 110, BP 104/62 (MAP 76), RR 18 (vent), SpO2 100%, temp 97.2 F, CPOT 2/8, RASS -3.

**Assessment and Disposition**
22% TBSA flame burn with inhalation injury and CO poisoning, acute respiratory failure s/p intubation, burn shock. Admitted to Burn ICU under Dr. Okafor with intensivist Dr. Brandt co-managing. Full code. Partner Jenna Whitaker updated at bedside. Report to ICU RN and transport to the Burn ICU at 04:00 on monitor with RT.

title: Procedure Note: Endotracheal Intubation
author: M. Castellano, MD
summary: RSI with etomidate and rocuronium, 8.0 ETT placed at 24 cm at 02:50 for inhalation injury with impending airway obstruction.
body:
**Procedure**
Emergent orotracheal intubation, rapid sequence induction.

**Indication**
Inhalation injury with facial burns, hoarse voice, developing stridor, singed nasal hair and oropharyngeal soot. High risk of progressive airway edema as resuscitation fluids begin.

**Consent and Time-out**
Emergent, implied consent; patient alert but airway at risk. Time-out performed with A. Torres, RN and RT.

**Preparation**
- Preoxygenation with 100% O2 by NRB for more than 3 minutes. Monitor: HR 122, BP 128/78 (MAP 95), SpO2 100% (not reliable, COHb pending). Suction, bougie, video laryngoscope and surgical airway kit at bedside. Two smaller ETT sizes available given expected edema. No cervical spine concern (no trauma).

**Medications (02:50)**
Etomidate 20 mg IV, rocuronium 100 mg IV.

**Technique**
Direct laryngoscopy with a Macintosh blade. Grade 2 view with edematous, erythematous supraglottic mucosa and soot. First pass success. 8.0 cuffed ETT placed 24 cm at the teeth. Cuff inflated to 24 cm H2O.

**Confirmation**
Positive waveform capnography, bilateral breath sounds, symmetric chest rise, condensation in the tube. SpO2 remained 100% throughout; no desaturation, hypotension or arrhythmia. Tube secured with commercial holder. Black sooty secretions suctioned.

**Initial Ventilator Settings**
AC/VC VT 450 mL (6 mL/kg IBW), RR 16, PEEP 5, FiO2 1.0. PIP 28, Pplat 21.

**Post-intubation**
Propofol infusion and fentanyl ordered for sedation. OG tube being placed. Portable CXR ordered to confirm ETT position (tip to be 3-5 cm above the carina).

**Complications**
None. Estimated blood loss none.

title: Procedure Note: Escharotomy, Right Forearm and Hand
author: R. Okafor, MD
summary: Bedside escharotomy of the right forearm and hand at 03:15 for compartment-like findings; Doppler signals returned; chest escharotomy not needed.
body:
**Procedure**
Bedside escharotomy, right forearm and hand.

**Indication**
Circumferential full-thickness burn of the right forearm and hand with a tense forearm, absent Doppler signals to the hand and increasing pain, concerning for compartment syndrome and vascular compromise from unyielding eschar during resuscitation.

**Consent**
Emergent; patient intubated and sedated. Partner Jenna Whitaker informed at bedside.

**Technique**
Sterile prep and drape with chlorhexidine, patient sedated on propofol and fentanyl with additional fentanyl given by the ED team. Mid-lateral and mid-medial incisions were made through the eschar with electrocautery, down to viable subcutaneous tissue, from the proximal forearm across the wrist and onto the hand, then along the thenar and hypothenar regions. Digits were not incised. Eschar edges released with immediate visible gaping and softening of the forearm.

**Findings and Result**
- Forearm compartments soft after release. Doppler signals returned at the radial and ulnar arteries and palmar arch, and signals present in the digits. Cap refill under 3 seconds.
- Bleeding about 150 mL, controlled with electrocautery and pressure. Vitals during the case: HR 112-116, BP 110/68 (MAP 82) at 03:20.

**Dressing and Aftercare**
- Incisions dressed with non-adherent gauze and loose wrap, fingertips left visible. Hand splinted in position of function and the arm elevated above heart level on pillows.
- Neurovascular checks (Doppler signal, cap refill, color, warmth, tension) hourly; call burn team immediately for loss of Doppler signal, pallor, tense forearm or escalating pain.

**Chest**
Anterior chest burn reviewed. Escharotomy not required: burn is anterior only, ventilation is adequate with PIP 28 and no restrictive chest wall findings. Will reassess if PIP rises.

**Complications**
None. Tolerated well.

**Plan**
Admit Burn ICU. Full burn H&P to follow.

title: Procedure Note: Central Venous Catheter, Left IJ
author: M. Castellano, MD
summary: Ultrasound-guided left IJ 7 Fr triple-lumen CVC placed at 03:45 under full barrier precautions; CXR to confirm tip.
body:
**Procedure**
Central venous catheter placement, left internal jugular vein, 7 Fr triple lumen.

**Indication**
Large-volume burn resuscitation (22% TBSA), burned right arm limiting peripheral access, possible need for vasoactive infusions and sedation drips.

**Consent**
Emergent; patient sedated and intubated.

**Technique**
- Site chosen at the left neck where skin is unburned (right neck and anterior chest burned). Time-out done. Hand hygiene, sterile full-barrier precautions (cap, mask, sterile gown and gloves, full body drape). Chlorhexidine skin prep, allowed to dry.
- Ultrasound with sterile probe cover: left IJ vein patent, compressible, lateral to carotid. Local lidocaine 1% 4 mL. Real-time ultrasound-guided needle entry on first pass with dark nonpulsatile blood return, guidewire advanced without resistance (no ectopy on monitor), skin nick, dilation, catheter advanced over the wire to 16 cm at the skin.
- All three lumens aspirate blood and flush easily. Sutured in place with chlorhexidine-impregnated dressing, line date on dressing.

**Findings**
Blood return from all lumens. No arrhythmia. Estimated blood loss under 5 mL. Vitals during procedure: HR 112, BP 106/64 (MAP 78), SpO2 100%.

**Confirmation**
Portable chest x-ray ordered for tip position and pneumothorax before use of the catheter for vasoactive or hyperosmolar infusions. Ultrasound of the lung showed lung sliding bilaterally.

**Complications**
None apparent.

**Plan**
CXR to confirm; central line care bundle; daily necessity review. Patient to Burn ICU.

title: Portable Chest X-ray, Post-intubation
author: Radiology Department
summary: ETT 4 cm above the carina, OG tube in stomach, lungs clear with mild perihilar haze.
body:
**Exam**
Portable AP chest radiograph, supine, 03:20.

**Indication**
Post-intubation and OG tube placement; inhalation injury.

**Comparison**
None.

**Findings**
- Endotracheal tube tip 4 cm above the carina. Orogastric tube courses below the diaphragm with the tip in the stomach. ECG leads and burn dressings overlie the chest.
- Lungs are clear. Mild perihilar haziness bilaterally. No focal consolidation, effusion or pneumothorax.
- Cardiomediastinal silhouette normal. No acute osseous abnormality.
impression: ETT tip 4 cm above carina in good position. OG tube tip in stomach. Lungs clear with mild perihilar haze; no pneumothorax.

title: Portable Chest X-ray, Post Central Line
author: Radiology Department
summary: Left IJ tip at cavo-atrial junction, no pneumothorax, mild bibasilar atelectasis and perihilar haze consistent with smoke inhalation.
body:
**Exam**
Portable AP chest radiograph, supine, 04:10.

**Indication**
Confirm position of left internal jugular central venous catheter.

**Comparison**
Portable chest radiograph 03:20.

**Findings**
- Left IJ central venous catheter tip at the cavo-atrial junction. No pneumothorax.
- Endotracheal tube tip 4 cm above the carina, unchanged. Orogastric tube tip in stomach.
- Mild bibasilar atelectasis. Mild perihilar haziness, slightly more conspicuous than prior, consistent with smoke inhalation. No effusion.
study: Portable chest x-ray, AP, after left IJ central line
impression: Left IJ CVC tip at cavo-atrial junction; no pneumothorax. ETT and OG tube in good position. Mild bibasilar atelectasis and perihilar haze, consistent with smoke inhalation.

title: Procedure Note: Arterial Line, Left Radial
author: L. Brandt, MD
summary: Left radial 20 g arterial line placed at 04:30 for continuous BP and frequent ABGs.
body:
**Procedure**
Arterial catheter placement, left radial artery, 20 gauge.

**Indication**
Hemodynamic monitoring during burn resuscitation with expected hypermetabolic changes and edema (noninvasive cuff unreliable), q4h arterial blood gases and lactate, mechanical ventilation.

**Consent**
Emergent/implied; patient sedated. Partner informed at bedside.

**Technique**
Right arm is burned, so the left was used. Modified Allen test normal (palmar flush within 5 seconds with ulnar compression). Time-out performed. Wrist positioned in dorsiflexion, chlorhexidine prep, sterile gloves and drape, lidocaine 1% 1 mL local. 20 g catheter placed at 04:30 with pulsatile flash on the first attempt, advanced over the wire. Connected to pressure tubing with 300 mmHg pressure bag, transducer leveled and zeroed at the phlebostatic axis. Sutured and dressed.

**Findings**
Good arterial waveform, no dampening. Arterial pressure correlates with cuff pressure (MAP about 70-72 mmHg). Left hand pink, warm, cap refill under 2 seconds; no ischemic changes after placement.

**Complications**
None; minimal bleeding.

**Plan**
Check left hand perfusion every 2 hours; zero and level each shift and with position change; daily necessity review. Draw q4h ABG and lactate from line.

title: Procedure Note: Bronchoscopy
author: L. Brandt, MD
summary: Bronchoscopy through ETT at 04:20 shows grade 2 inhalation injury; airway cleared and inhalation injury protocol started.
body:
**Procedure**
Flexible fiberoptic bronchoscopy through the endotracheal tube, performed at 04:20.

**Indication**
Evaluation and grading of inhalation injury after enclosed-space fire exposure, soot in the airway; pulmonary toilet.

**Sedation and Monitoring**
On propofol 30 mcg/kg/min and fentanyl 100 mcg/h, RASS -3. FiO2 1.0 maintained throughout. HR 106, BP 101/58 (MAP 72), SpO2 100%. Airway pressures monitored.

**Findings**
- ETT 24 cm at the teeth, tip about 4 cm above the carina. Vocal cords edematous; supraglottic mucosal erythema and edema.
- Trachea and mainstem bronchi: diffuse erythema, soot deposition and mucosal edema. No ulceration or mucosal sloughing. No carbonaceous casts below the carina. Thick sooty secretions in the trachea and right mainstem bronchus.
- Abbreviated Injury Score grade 2 (mild-moderate) inhalation injury.

**Intervention**
Sooty secretions suctioned and the airway cleared with saline lavage aliquots. No culture sent (no sign of infection). Scope withdrawn without complication.

**Post-procedure**
PIP unchanged at 28, Pplat 21, SpO2 100%.

**Inhalation Injury Protocol Started**
- Albuterol 2.5 mg neb q4h.
- Nebulized heparin 5,000 units q8h alternating every 4 hours with nebulized N-acetylcysteine 20% 3 mL q8h.
- Chest physiotherapy and pulmonary toilet with frequent suctioning. Head of bed 30 degrees.

**Plan**
Continue lung-protective ventilation; wean FiO2 as COHb clears. Repeat bronchoscopy only if clinical change.

title: Burn Surgery History and Physical
author: R. Okafor, MD
summary: Burn surgery admission H&P: 22% TBSA flame burn with inhalation injury, post-escharotomy, Parkland resuscitation in progress.
body:
**Chief Complaint**
Flame burns and smoke inhalation after a house fire.

**HPI**
34-year-old right-hand-dominant male HVAC technician. At about 01:30 Monday he fell asleep on the couch after drinking and smoking, woke to smoke and re-entered the enclosed house to carry his 6-year-old daughter out. He sustained flame burns to the right arm and chest and inhaled smoke. Found outside by firefighters. EMS gave O2 and 500 mL LR. In the ED (arrival 02:30) he was hoarse with stridor, soot and singed nasal hair, and was intubated at 02:50. COHb 14.2%. Right forearm escharotomy at 03:15 for tense forearm and absent hand Doppler signals; signals returned. Left IJ CVC 03:45, left radial arterial line 04:30, bronchoscopy 04:20 showed grade 2 inhalation injury. Tdap given 03:30. ICU arrival 04:00.

**PMH / PSH**
Childhood asthma (resolved, no inhalers as an adult), seasonal allergies. No prior surgeries.

**Medications / Allergies**
Cetirizine PRN only. No known drug allergies.

**Social**
Lives with partner Jenna Whitaker (health care proxy discussed) and daughter Ava, 6, both uninjured. Alcohol 4-6 beers on weekends, more on the night of injury (ethanol 42 mg/dL at 02:40). Tobacco 1 ppd x 15 years (15 pack-years). No illicit drugs; urine drug screen negative.

**Review of Systems**
Unobtainable, intubated and sedated. Per ED history no chest pain prior to the fire.

**Vitals (05:00)**
HR 109, BP 99/55 (MAP 70), RR 18 (vent), SpO2 99% (not reliable with COHb), temp 97.6 F, weight 82 kg, height 180 cm.

**Exam**
- General: intubated, sedated, RASS -3. HEENT: facial burns, singed brows and nasal hair, perioral soot, lips edematous. Neck: ETT secured. Lungs: coarse bilateral breath sounds, PIP 28. CV: tachycardic, regular. Abdomen: soft, OG tube in place.
- Right hand: Doppler signals present at radial, ulnar and digital arteries after escharotomy; cap refill 2 seconds; forearm soft. Left arm/legs unburned.

**Burn Map (TBSA 22%, about 8% full thickness)**
- Right arm circumferential 9%: forearm and hand full thickness, upper arm deep partial.
- Anterior chest 9%: deep partial with scattered full-thickness patches.
- Face and neck 4%: superficial to superficial-partial.

**Data**
Lactate 5.8 -> 3.4 (04:15). COHb 14.2% -> 6.4% (04:15). ABG 04:15 pH 7.34, PaCO2 40, PaO2 288. Cr 0.9, K 4.3, CK 480, troponin 0.02. CXR 04:10: ETT, OG, left IJ tip cavo-atrial, no pneumothorax.

**Assessment and Resuscitation Plan**
22% TBSA flame burn with grade 2 inhalation injury and CO exposure in burn shock.
- Parkland: 4 mL x 82 kg x 22% = 7,216 mL LR in 24 h from injury (01:30 to 01:30 Tuesday). 3,608 mL in the first 8 h (to 09:30); EMS 500 mL counted, so 3,108 mL over 7 h = 444 mL/h; currently 450 mL/h. Second half 3,608 mL over 16 h (225 mL/h from 09:30).
- Titrate to UOP 30-50 mL/h (0.5 mL/kg/h = 41 mL/h). UOP so far 25 mL/h (04:00-05:00); if under 30 for 2 consecutive hours, raise rate 20-25%; if over 50 for 2 hours, reduce. Watch for fluid creep. Bladder pressure q6h.

**Wound Care Plan**
Initial cleansing and first dressing change at 14:00 with burn nurse: silver sulfadiazine 1% to chest and right arm daily; bacitracin ointment to face BID. Hourly neurovascular checks of the right hand. Arm elevated, hand splinted in position of function.

**Other**
- Tetanus: Tdap given 03:30. Nutrition: trophic tube feeds this morning, dietitian consult. Stress ulcer and VTE prophylaxis. Pain/sedation per ICU. Contact precautions.
- OR: excision and autografting of the full-thickness right forearm/hand and chest areas planned in several days once resuscitation is complete; tentatively Friday 11-06.
- Consults: critical care (Dr. Brandt), RD, PT/OT, case management/social work, pharmacy.

**Disposition**
Burn ICU, full code. Plan discussed with Jenna Whitaker at bedside.

title: Portable Chest X-ray, ICU Day 1
author: Radiology Department
summary: Small RLL atelectasis, otherwise clear lungs, lines and tubes in good position.
body:
**Exam**
Portable AP chest radiograph, supine, 05:15 Tuesday (daily ICU film).

**Comparison**
Portable chest radiograph 04:10 Monday.

**Findings**
- Endotracheal tube tip 4 cm above the carina. Orogastric tube tip in the stomach. Left IJ central venous catheter tip at the cavo-atrial junction. No pneumothorax.
- Small right lower lobe atelectasis, new. Perihilar haze has improved. Left lung clear. No pleural effusion, no pulmonary edema, no consolidation.
- Cardiomediastinal silhouette normal.
study: Portable chest x-ray, AP, ICU day 1 daily film
impression: Small RLL atelectasis, otherwise clear. ETT, OG tube and left IJ CVC in good position. No pneumothorax or edema.

title: Respiratory Therapy Initial Evaluation
author: D. Alvarez, RRT
summary: RT initial evaluation: AC/VC with FiO2 1.0, grade 2 inhalation injury, COHb 6.4% on 04:15 ABG, FiO2 weaning plan, inhalation protocol and VAP bundle started.
body:
**Reason for Evaluation**
34 M, 82 kg, 180 cm (IBW 75 kg), intubated 02:50 in ED for inhalation injury with 22% TBSA burns. Arrived Burn ICU 04:00.

**Airway**
Oral 8.0 ETT, 24 cm at the teeth, secured with commercial holder. CXR 04:10: tip 4 cm above carina. Cuff pressure 24 cm H2O (goal 20-30), checked q shift and with tube repositioning. Bronchoscopy 04:20 (Dr. Brandt): grade 2 inhalation injury, soot cleared.

**Ventilator Settings and Mechanics**
- AC/VC, VT 450 mL (6 mL/kg IBW), set RR 16, PEEP 5, FiO2 1.0. Total RR 17-18.
- PIP 28, Pplat 21 cm H2O; driving pressure 16; static compliance about 28 mL/cmH2O. Plateau under 30 goal met.
- Breath sounds coarse with scattered rhonchi, improved after bronchoscopy and suctioning. Secretions: moderate, thick, black-tinged, decreasing.

**ABG 04:15 (FiO2 1.0)**
pH 7.34, PaCO2 40, PaO2 288, HCO3 21, BE -4, O2 sat 94%, COHb 6.4% (14.2% at 02:50), lactate 3.4. P/F 288. SpO2 on monitor 100% overestimates oxygen content while COHb is elevated; use ABG co-oximetry.

**FiO2 Weaning Plan**
- Keep FiO2 1.0 while COHb is elevated (half-life of COHb about 60-90 min on 100% O2). Order received to wean to 0.60 at 06:00, goal PaO2 80-120 and SpO2 94% or higher; ABG with COHb at 08:00 before further weaning. Continue wean by 0.10 q2-4h as gases allow; target FiO2 0.40 by tomorrow if COHb under 3%.

**Inhalation Injury Protocol**
- Albuterol 2.5 mg neb q4h. Nebulized heparin 5,000 units in 3 mL saline and nebulized N-acetylcysteine 20% 3 mL, each q8h, alternated every 4 hours (heparin 07:00, 15:00, 23:00; NAC 11:00, 19:00, 03:00). Chest physiotherapy and suction q2-4h and PRN.

**VAP Bundle**
- HOB 30 degrees or higher, oral care with chlorhexidine 0.12% BID plus toothbrushing q12h, suction as needed (no subglottic suction ETT), closed in-line suction, daily SAT/SBT assessment, VTE and stress ulcer prophylaxis, circuit changes only if soiled, cuff pressure q shift.

**Plan**
RT to follow q4h with settings check, daily CXR review, SBT screen when FiO2 under 0.50 and PEEP 5-8. Will notify Dr. Brandt for PIP over 35, Pplat over 30, or new secretions.

title: Critical Care Admission History and Physical
author: L. Brandt, MD
summary: ICU admission H&P: 22% TBSA burn with inhalation injury, CO exposure, ventilated respiratory failure and burn shock, plan by system.
body:
**Reason for ICU Admission**
Burn shock and acute hypoxemic respiratory failure after 22% TBSA flame burn with smoke inhalation.

**HPI**
34-year-old male with history of childhood asthma, 15 pack-year smoker, who was injured in a house fire at 01:30 after drinking alcohol. Went back into the house to carry his 6-year-old daughter out. EMS gave 100% O2 and 500 mL LR. ED arrival 02:30: hoarse, stridor, soot; intubated 02:50 (etomidate/rocuronium, 8.0 ETT 24 cm). COHb 14.2%, lactate 5.8, ethanol 42. Right forearm escharotomy 03:15 (burn surgery). Left IJ CVC 03:45, arterial line 04:30, bronchoscopy 04:20: grade 2 inhalation injury. Arrived Burn ICU 04:00. Full code.

**PMH / Meds / Allergies / Social**
Childhood asthma (resolved), seasonal allergies. Cetirizine PRN. NKDA. Alcohol on weekends. Lives with partner Jenna Whitaker (at bedside) and daughter Ava (6, uninjured).

**Vitals (05:00)**
HR 109, BP 99/55 (MAP 70), RR 18 (set 16), SpO2 99%, temp 97.6 F. Vent AC/VC 450/16, PEEP 5, FiO2 1.0, PIP 28, Pplat 21. LR 450 mL/h. Propofol 30 mcg/kg/min, fentanyl 100 mcg/h. UOP 25 mL/h (04:00-05:00). RASS -3, CPOT 1.

**Exam**
Sedated, RASS -3, no distress. Facial burns and soot, ETT in place. Coarse breath sounds bilaterally, no wheeze now. Tachycardic, regular, cap refill 3 sec. Abdomen soft, nondistended. Right forearm/hand escharotomy incisions dressed, Doppler signals present. No focal neuro deficits (moves left arm and both legs to pain).

**Labs / Imaging**
02:40: WBC 12.8, Hgb 17.2, Plt 288, Na 138, K 4.3, CO2 19, BUN 14, Cr 0.9, glucose 143, INR 1.1, ethanol 42, CK 480, troponin 0.02. ABG 04:15: 7.34/40/288/21, BE -4, COHb 6.4%, lactate 3.4 (5.8 at 02:50). POC glucose 148. CXR 04:10: ETT, OG and left IJ tip cavo-atrial junction good; no PTX; mild bibasilar atelectasis/perihilar haze.

**ICU Problem List**
1. Inhalation injury (grade 2) and CO poisoning.
2. Acute hypoxemic respiratory failure on mechanical ventilation.
3. Burn shock / resuscitation.
4. Sedation and analgesia.
5. Hyperglycemia risk / glucose control.
6. VTE prophylaxis.
7. Stress ulcer prophylaxis.
8. Nutrition.
9. Lines and tubes.
10. Alcohol use.

**Assessment and Plan by System**
- Neuro: Propofol 30 mcg/kg/min and fentanyl 100 mcg/h, RASS goal -2 to -3 today (-1 to -2 Tuesday), CPOT hourly, treat 4 or higher. Daily SAT starting Tuesday. Thiamine/folate for alcohol use; monitor for withdrawal, avoid benzodiazepines when possible.
- Resp: Lung-protective ventilation VT 6 mL/kg IBW (450), Pplat under 30. Wean FiO2 to 0.60 at 06:00; COHb and ABG 08:00; continue 100% O2 until COHb under 3-5%. Inhalation protocol (albuterol, nebulized heparin, NAC), chest PT. HOB 30 degrees, chlorhexidine oral care, daily CXR at 05:00.
- CV/shock: Burn shock with lactate 3.4 (from 5.8). Parkland LR 450 mL/h, titrate to UOP 30-50 mL/h. MAP goal 65 or higher. Cyanide toxicity considered (lactate, soot) but improving with fluids and oxygen; no hydroxocobalamin. Troponin repeat (second troponin due this morning).
- Renal: CK 480; UA myoglobin negative; follow CK x3, BMP/Mg/Phos q6h, bladder pressure q6h.
- GI: OG tube. Trophic feeds Osmolite 1.5 at 20 mL/h at 10:00, advance 10 mL/h q4h to 70 mL/h. Pantoprazole 40 mg IV daily from 09:00.
- Heme: Hgb 17.2 hemoconcentrated; CBC q12h. Heparin 5,000 units SQ q8h (first dose 06:00).
- ID: Tdap given. No prophylactic systemic antibiotics. Topical SSD/bacitracin per burn team.
- Endo: Glucose 143-148; POC q6h, start insulin infusion if persistently over 180.
- Lines: Left IJ CVC (03:45), left radial A-line (04:30), left AC 18 g PIV, OG, Foley (02:45), ETT 24 cm.
- Prophylaxis/Dispo: Burn ICU, full code, contact precautions, family updated.

Critical care time spent: 45 minutes.

title: Pharmacy Admission Note
author: A. Chen, PharmD
summary: Pharmacy admission review: med rec, Parkland and drug dosing checks, sedation, prophylaxis and burn-specific monitoring.
body:
**Patient**
34 M, 82 kg (dosing weight), 180 cm, IBW 75 kg, 22% TBSA flame burn with inhalation injury, intubated. NKDA. Cr 0.9 (02:40, 06:00). Vitals at 07:00: HR 111, BP 99/57 (MAP 71), temp 98.2 F, UOP 33 mL/h (last hour).

**Medication Reconciliation**
Sources: partner Jenna Whitaker and chart. No home prescription medications. Cetirizine 10 mg PO PRN for seasonal allergies (hold while NPO). No herbals or supplements reported. No known allergies. Tobacco 1 ppd: nicotine withdrawal possible; offer patch if agitation or per MD. Alcohol use: thiamine, folate, MVI ordered.

**Parkland Check**
4 mL x 82 kg x 22% = 7,216 mL LR/24 h from 01:30. EMS 500 mL counted. LR 450 mL/h since 02:30; increased to 540 mL/h at 06:00 for UOP 25-26 mL/h x 2 h (goal 30-50 mL/h). Calculation verified; no bag labeling issues. Flag fluid creep risk.

**Sedation and Analgesia**
Propofol 30 mcg/kg/min (about 15 mL/h) provides about 390 kcal/day from lipid; baseline triglycerides needed (check Tuesday 06:00) and monitor for propofol infusion syndrome with prolonged high doses. Fentanyl 100 mcg/h (about 1.2 mcg/kg/h); burn patients often need higher opioid requirements and tolerance develops. Hydromorphone 0.5 mg IV for dressing changes. Avoid routine benzodiazepines (delirium).

**Stress Ulcer and VTE Prophylaxis**
Pantoprazole 40 mg IV daily (first dose 09:00) appropriate: ventilated, burn over 20% TBSA. Heparin 5,000 units SQ q8h (first dose 06:00); burn patients at high VTE risk. Platelets 288, baseline aPTT 29; monitor platelets at least every 48 h for HIT (also on nebulized heparin 5,000 units q8h; systemic absorption minimal but monitor aPTT).

**Acetaminophen**
1,000 mg IV q8h (3 g/day) scheduled. Max 4 g/day; given alcohol use, burn hypermetabolism and AST/ALT pending, cap at 3 g/day. Check LFTs Tuesday.

**Burn-specific Drug Issues**
- Early (first 48 h): decreased clearance and larger Vd (edema). After 48-72 h: hypermetabolic, increased renal and hepatic clearance, so beta-lactams and aminoglycosides may need higher or more frequent dosing, vancomycin levels more important. Hypoalbuminemia (3.8 now, falling with resuscitation) raises free fraction of highly bound drugs. Avoid IM/subcutaneous routes in burned tissue (erratic absorption); use IV or enteral.
- Rocuronium given 02:50; effect resolved by now (verify train of four if needed).
- Vitamin C 500 mg BID, zinc 220 mg daily and MVI per burn protocol; start with feeds at 09:00.

**Antimicrobial Plan**
No systemic prophylactic antibiotics. Topicals: silver sulfadiazine 1% daily (first application 14:00, monitor WBC for transient leukopenia); bacitracin ointment BID to face. Tdap given 03:30. Monitor for fever, wound changes; pharmacy ready to dose empiric therapy (vancomycin 20 mg/kg load, pip-tazo) if infection suspected.

**Monitoring**
BMP/Mg/Phos q6h, CBC q12h, LFTs/TG Tuesday, glucose, CK x3, COHb, daily weights not applicable while resuscitating. Pharmacy will follow daily.

title: Critical Care Progress Note, ICU Day 1
author: L. Brandt, MD
summary: ICU day 1 course: resuscitation on track with UOP in range, COHb cleared, FiO2 weaned to 0.50, plan overnight.
body:
**Subjective / Interval Events**
Patient intubated and sedated, RASS -3. Hydromorphone 0.5 mg given 13:45 for the 14:00 dressing change (CPOT 4, back to 1). Partner Jenna Whitaker and mother Linda Delaney at bedside, updated. No acute events.

**Objective (18:00)**
HR 98, BP 108/61 (MAP 77), RR 16, SpO2 99%, temp 99.1 F. A-line MAP 77. CPOT 1/8, RASS -3.

**Fluids**
- LR: EMS 500 mL, then 450 mL/h from 02:30, 540 mL/h from 06:00, 225 mL/h from 09:30, 270 mL/h from 14:00. Cumulative since injury about 6,190 mL (first 8 h 3,965 mL vs Parkland 3,608 mL). Feeds Osmolite 1.5 now 40 mL/h.
- I&O 04:00-18:00: total intake about 5,790 mL, urine 501 mL (about 36 mL/h, 0.44 mL/kg/h). Hourly UOP last 4 h: 37, 38, 42, 46 mL. Early UOP 25-26 mL/h at 04:00-06:00 prompted the rate increase to 540; UOP dipped to 28 mL/h at 12:00-13:00, rate 270 from 14:00. Bladder pressure 12 mmHg.
- Current rate 270 mL/h is above the 225 mL/h Parkland baseline; UOP in range, so no reduction yet; will reduce 20-25% if UOP over 50 mL/h x 2 h. Fluid creep discussed with Dr. Okafor.

**Respiratory**
AC/VC 450/16, PEEP 5, FiO2 0.50 since 14:00, PIP 27, Pplat 20. ABG 16:00: 7.40/38/128/24, lactate 1.6. COHb 6.4% (04:15) -> 3.1% (08:00) -> 3.0% (12:00). CO poisoning resolved. Inhalation protocol continues. Plan to wean FiO2 toward 0.40.

**Neuro**
Propofol 35 mcg/kg/min (increased from 30 at 16:00), fentanyl 100 mcg/h. RASS goal -2 to -3. SAT planned Tuesday.

**Labs**
12:00: WBC 16.1, Hgb 13.6, Plt 246, Na 136, K 4.9, CO2 22, BUN 17, Cr 1.0, glucose 172, Ca 8.1, iCa 1.05, CK 1,120 (480 at 02:50). Troponin 0.02 x2. 16:00 POC glucose 181. 18:00: Na 135, K 5.0, CO2 22, BUN 19, Cr 1.0, glucose 188, Ca 7.9, Mg 1.8, Phos 2.8.

**Assessment and Plan**
1. Inhalation injury / CO: COHb normalized; FiO2 wean, inhalation protocol, daily CXR.
2. Respiratory failure: lung-protective ventilation, wean FiO2 by 0.1 q4h for SpO2 94% or higher.
3. Burn shock: Parkland per UOP titration, MAP 77, lactate cleared.
4. Right hand: Doppler signals present hourly; hand warm.
5. Renal/CK: K 5.0 upper-normal, CK peaking 1,120; repeat BMP, CK at 00:00; watch ECG.
6. Glucose: 181-188; start insulin infusion if POC at 22:00 remains over 180.
7. Nutrition: feeds advancing; dietitian assessment done.
8. Prophylaxis: heparin SQ, pantoprazole, chlorhexidine oral care.
9. Overnight: hourly UOP and neurovascular checks, ABG 20:00, labs 00:00, reassess rates.

title: Critical Care Progress Note, ICU Day 2
author: L. Brandt, MD
summary: ICU day 2: resuscitation winding down, not ready for SBT, insulin infusion running, feeds at goal; SAT planned 08:00.
body:
**Interval Events**
- 00:30 insulin infusion started 1 unit/h for glucose 190-198; now 1.5 unit/h. 03:00 agitation with ETT despite sedation, lorazepam 1 mg IV x1; avoid further benzodiazepines. 04:00 propofol decreased to 30 mcg/kg/min, FiO2 0.40. 06:00 LR decreased to 75 mL/h and albumin 5% 500 mL over 4 h started; feeds at goal 70 mL/h.

**Objective (07:00)**
HR 96, BP 111/64 (MAP 80), RR 17, SpO2 98%, temp 99.4 F. AC/VC 450/16, PEEP 5, FiO2 0.40, PIP 24, Pplat 17. RASS -2, CPOT 1. Propofol 30, fentanyl 100 mcg/h. UOP last 6 h: 43, 42, 41, 44, 45, 47 mL/h (0.5-0.57 mL/kg/h). Total UOP 04:00 Mon to 07:00 Tue: 1,006 mL.

**Labs**
- ABG 06:00: 7.41/40/124/25, lactate 1.4. Na 134, K 3.9, Cl 108, CO2 24, BUN 23, Cr 1.1, glucose 177, Ca 7.7, iCa 1.02, Mg 1.6, Phos 2.1. Albumin 2.6 (05:00), AST 72, ALT 58, INR 1.2, fibrinogen 420, prealbumin 7.1, TG 168.
- 00:00: WBC 15.2, Hgb 12.4, Plt 214, CK 840. POC glucose 06:30 179.
- CXR 05:15: small RLL atelectasis, lines in position.

**Assessment and Plan**
1. Ventilator/readiness: FiO2 0.40, PEEP 5 meets thresholds, but not ready for SBT today given ongoing resuscitation and albumin infusion; SAT at 08:00 (propofol held, wake to RASS 0 to -1, fentanyl continued); re-evaluate SBT tomorrow. Goal RASS -1 to -2 today. HOB 30, chlorhexidine care, chest PT for RLL atelectasis.
2. Shock/fluids: resuscitation nearly complete; transition to maintenance with Dr. Okafor; MAP 80, lactate normal.
3. Glucose: insulin infusion to goal 140-180; hourly checks per protocol.
4. Electrolytes: Mg 1.6, Phos 2.1, K 3.9; replete per protocol if noon BMP confirms; liver enzymes mildly up (shock/EtOH/propofol), repeat.
5. Nutrition: Osmolite 1.5 at goal 70 mL/h (about 2,500 kcal, 105 g protein); residuals q4h.
6. Delirium prevention: CAM-ICU q shift, avoid benzodiazepines, family orientation, sleep-wake cycle.
7. ID: afebrile (99.4 F); WBC 15.2 (stress); no antibiotics.
8. Lines: left IJ CVC day 2, A-line day 2, PIV; Foley day 2 still needed.
9. Prophylaxis: heparin 5,000 units SQ q8h, pantoprazole.

title: Burn Surgery Progress Note
author: R. Okafor, MD
summary: Day 2 burn rounds: 24 h resuscitation total about 8,080 mL vs 7,216 mL goal (12% over), wounds clean, transition to maintenance, OR tentatively Fri 11-06.
body:
**24-hour Resuscitation**
- Goal 4 mL x 82 kg x 22% = 7,216 mL LR; first 8 h goal 3,608 mL. Actual crystalloid from injury 01:30 to 01:30 Tuesday about 8,080 mL (12% over); first 8 h about 3,965 mL (10% over). Contributing: rate increased to 540 mL/h at 06:00 and 270 mL/h from 14:00 for UOP in the high 20s to low 30s. Edema moderate, peak airway pressures fell (PIP 28 to 24), bladder pressure 10-14 mmHg. Fluid creep reviewed with the ICU team.
- UOP 04:00 Monday to now 1,006 mL; last 6 h 41-47 mL/h (0.5-0.57 mL/kg/h). Lactate 1.4.

**Interval / Overnight**
Hemodynamically stable. LR decreased to 125 mL/h at 01:30, 75 mL/h at 06:00 with albumin 5% 500 mL over 4 h. Glucose 177-198, insulin infusion running.

**Wound Exam (dressings taken down at rounds)**
- Right forearm and hand: dry tan-white leathery full thickness, insensate. Escharotomy incisions clean, edges gaping, minimal serosanguinous ooze. Forearm soft. Doppler signals present radial/ulnar and digital, cap refill 2 sec, fingertips warm and pink.
- Right upper arm: deep partial, mottled with ruptured blisters, moist, no odor or purulence.
- Anterior chest: deep partial with scattered full-thickness patches (about 3 cm), no spreading erythema. Face and neck: superficial-partial, erythema with weeping blisters, improving on bacitracin.
- Eyes clear. No signs of infection. Afebrile 99.4 F.

**Labs**
Na 134, K 3.9, Cr 1.1, Mg 1.6, Phos 2.1, albumin 2.6, WBC 15.2, Hgb 12.4, Plt 214, CK 840 (falling).

**Assessment and Plan**
22% TBSA flame burn, ICU day 2, post-escharotomy.
1. Resuscitation: convert from Parkland to maintenance. LR 75 mL/h while albumin 5% 500 mL runs (06:00-10:00), then LR 100 mL/h from 10:00, titrate UOP 0.5-1 mL/kg/h; albumin for hypoalbuminemia per protocol.
2. Wounds: daily dressing change 14:00 with silver sulfadiazine to chest and right arm, bacitracin BID face. Hourly neurovascular checks right hand today.
3. OR: excision and autografting of right forearm/hand and chest tentatively Friday 11-06; consent from patient when he can participate or Jenna Whitaker as proxy. Hold feeds only per anesthesia.
4. Nutrition: tube feeds at goal, vitamin C/zinc/MVI, protein modular if needed; follow prealbumin.
5. Pain: hydromorphone pre-dressing. PT/OT for splinting and ROM.
6. ICU rounds with Dr. Brandt done; daily communication with Jenna.

title: Initial Nutrition Assessment
author: P. Moreno, RD
summary: Initial RD assessment for 22% TBSA burn on ventilator: needs about 2,450 kcal and 1.5-2 g/kg protein, trophic feeds started 10:00, micronutrient plan, refeeding risk.
body:
**Reason for Assessment**
Hypermetabolic 22% TBSA flame burn with inhalation injury, intubated, RD consult within 24 h.

**Anthropometrics**
Height 180 cm, weight 82 kg (admission, pre-resuscitation; dosing weight 82 kg), IBW 75 kg (109% IBW), BMI 25.3. Weight now unreliable due to resuscitation edema. No recent weight loss per partner; well nourished before injury.

**Nutrition-relevant History**
No GI history. Alcohol 4-6 beers on weekends (more on the night of injury; ethanol 42 mg/dL), tobacco 1 ppd. Normal diet, independent. NKDA.

**Current Nutrition Support**
NPO, OG tube 16 Fr (CXR confirmed). Osmolite 1.5 started 10:00 at 20 mL/h (trophic), advance 10 mL/h q4h (30 mL/h at 14:00) to goal 70 mL/h, expected around 06:00 Tuesday. Free water flush 30 mL q4h. No GI intolerance; residuals not an issue so far, abdomen soft. HOB 30 degrees. Do not hold feeds for dressing changes.

**Estimated Needs**
- Energy: about 2,450 kcal/day (Toronto-type hypermetabolic estimate, about 30 kcal/kg); Curreri formula (25 kcal/kg + 40 kcal x %TBSA) gives about 2,930 kcal and tends to overestimate, so not used.
- Protein: 1.5-2 g/kg = 123-164 g/day (goal about 130 g). Goal feeds provide 2,520 kcal and 105 g protein; add protein modular (e.g., 4 packets/day, about 24 g) to reach about 130 g.
- Propofol 30 mcg/kg/min supplies about 390 kcal/day from lipid; count it. Will reassess goal rate on Tuesday with propofol dose and prealbumin.
- Fluid per resuscitation protocol.

**Labs (12:00, 18:00 pending)**
Na 136, K 4.9, Cl 105, CO2 22, BUN 17, Cr 1.0, glucose 172, Ca 8.1, Mg 1.9, Phos 3.0. Albumin 3.8 (admission; will fall with resuscitation and is not a nutrition marker). CK 1,120. Lactate 1.8. Triglycerides and prealbumin planned Tuesday.

**Micronutrients**
Ascorbic acid 500 mg BID, zinc sulfate 220 mg daily, multivitamin with minerals daily, thiamine 100 mg and folic acid 1 mg daily started 09:00. Monitor Cu/Se levels later in stay.

**Refeeding Risk**
Moderate: alcohol use, burn stress. Thiamine given before feeds. Monitor K, Mg, Phos q6h (Phos 3.0 now); replete before advancing if Phos under 2.5. Advance feeds per schedule.

**Glycemic**
Glucose 164-181, goal 140-180. Insulin infusion if persistently over 180 per ICU.

**Plan**
1. Continue advance to goal 70 mL/h. 2. Protein modular at goal. 3. Daily RD follow-up; nitrogen balance when able. 4. Weekly weights when edema resolves. 5. Transition to oral supplements after extubation and swallow screen.

title: Burn Wound Assessment and Dressing Change
author: N. Ibarra, RN
summary: First 14:00 dressing change: wounds by area, no signs of infection, silver sulfadiazine applied, pain premedicated.
body:
**Reason**
Daily burn wound assessment and dressing change at 14:00 with J. Morales, RN. 22% TBSA flame burn. Sterile technique, gown, gloves, mask.

**Pain Management**
Hydromorphone 0.5 mg IV given 13:45. CPOT 4/8 at 14:00 during removal of dressings (grimace, tense muscle tone), 1/8 by 15:00. Continuous fentanyl 100 mcg/h and propofol 30 mcg/kg/min running. RASS -3.

**Vitals**
14:00 HR 102, BP 108/63 (MAP 78), RR 18, SpO2 99%, temp 99.0 F. 15:00 HR 102, BP 107/62 (MAP 77).

**Wound Description by Area**
- Right forearm and hand (circumferential, 3rd degree): leathery, waxy white to tan, dry, nonblanching, insensate to pinprick; escharotomy incisions mid-medial and mid-lateral from forearm across wrist and hand, edges gaping, clean red-pink fat, scant serosanguinous ooze, no active bleeding. Fingers edematous, pink at tips, cap refill 2 sec, Doppler signals radial/ulnar and digital present.
- Right upper arm (deep partial): mottled red and white, ruptured blisters, moist, slow cap refill, no odor.
- Anterior chest (deep partial with scattered full-thickness patches): pale/white-tan areas about 3 cm each, surrounding deep red moist tissue. Drainage scant to moderate serosanguinous.
- Face and neck: superficial-partial, erythema, intact and ruptured blisters on cheeks and forehead, brows singed, lips edematous, no eschar.
- No purulence, no foul odor, no surrounding spreading erythema.

**Care Provided**
Dressings soaked off with saline; wounds cleansed with mild soap and sterile water, loose blisters debrided per protocol. Silver sulfadiazine 1% applied about 1/16 inch thick to the right arm and chest. Covered with non-adherent layer, gauze and loose wrap, fingers wrapped separately with tips visible. Bacitracin to face. Photos taken in the chart media (measurements recorded). Total time about 40 minutes.

**Positioning / Splint**
Right hand splinted in position of function, arm elevated above heart on pillows. Turn side to side without lying on the right arm or chest.

**Response**
Tolerated with transient HR rise. No bleeding. Dressing intact.

**Plan**
Daily change at 14:00 with premedication 15 min before. Hourly neurovascular checks. Watch for fever, odor, purulence, spreading erythema (mark margins), eschar separation. Burn nurse specialist to follow daily. Jenna Whitaker updated.

title: Physical Therapy Initial Evaluation
author: S. Kim, PT
summary: PT evaluation: intubated and sedated, passive ROM program, positioning to prevent contractures, baseline fully independent.
body:
**Reason for Referral**
Burn rehabilitation, 22% TBSA right arm and chest burns, ventilated, ICU day 1.

**Prior Level of Function**
Independent in all mobility and ADLs, working full time as an HVAC technician (ladders, crawl spaces, lifting 50-75 lb), right-hand dominant. Lived in a single-story house with partner and daughter. Source: partner.

**Current Status**
Intubated, sedated (RASS -3), unable to participate. Vitals 15:00: HR 102, BP 107/62 (MAP 77), SpO2 99% on FiO2 0.50. Lines: ETT, left IJ CVC, left radial A-line, OG, Foley. Right forearm escharotomy dressings, hand splinted, arm elevated. Strength and sensation unable to test; moves left arm and legs to stimulation.

**Contraindications / Precautions**
- No active exercise while sedated. No stretching across fresh escharotomy incisions or wrist/hand without burn team clearance. Avoid pressure on chest wall and right arm. Hold ROM if MAP under 65, HR over 130, or new arrhythmia. Maintain ETT and line safety, heel offloading. No OOB during resuscitation.

**Plan / Interventions**
- Passive ROM, 10 reps BID, with RN present: left upper extremity and both lower extremities all planes; right shoulder (flexion/abduction to 90 degrees), right elbow to full extension within tolerance. Coordinate premedication with dressing changes.
- Positioning: shoulders abducted about 90 degrees, elbow extended, neck neutral with no pillow behind head if neck contracture risk, ankles neutral with foot positioners to prevent plantarflexion contracture, knees extended.
- Pulmonary support with RT; early mobility progression once resuscitation done: sitting at bedside, then chair.

**Goals**
Short term (1 week): maintain full passive ROM, no contractures, tolerate dangle. Long term: independent household ambulation and return to work with right hand function.

**Frequency**
Daily 5x/week. Discussed positioning with RN. Jenna Whitaker informed of therapy plan.

title: Occupational Therapy Initial Evaluation
author: H. Larsen, OTR/L
summary: OT evaluation: right hand splint in position of function, edema control and elevation, ADL baseline independent.
body:
**Reason for Referral**
Right hand and forearm full-thickness burn s/p escharotomy; splinting, edema and ADL planning.

**Prior Level of Function**
Right-hand dominant, independent in ADLs, IADLs and work as an HVAC technician. Lives with partner Jenna Whitaker and daughter Ava (6).

**Current Status**
Intubated and sedated (RASS -3), HR 102, BP 107/62 (MAP 77). Right hand: marked edema, dressings in place, fingers pink, cap refill about 2 sec, Doppler signals present; cannot assess active movement or sensation. Left hand intact, A-line left wrist.

**Splinting**
Pre-fabricated resting splint applied overnight reviewed and remolded: right volar resting hand splint in the position of safe function: wrist neutral to slight extension (about 20 degrees), MCP joints 60-70 degrees flexion, IP joints extended, thumb abducted with web space open. Padding over wrist incisions, straps loose to avoid pressure, fingertips visible. Skin checked under straps at each dressing change; splint on at all times except dressing changes and therapy.

**Edema Management**
Hand and arm elevated above heart level on pillows/foam wedge; fingertips visible for hourly checks. No compression until burn team approves. Gentle active range when awake.

**ADL / Cognitive Baseline**
Independent in self-care. No cognitive concerns prior to injury; ETOH use noted. Will reassess after extubation.

**Goals**
Maintain MCP flexion and web space, prevent claw hand, minimize edema; independent feeding and grooming with adaptive equipment and left hand within 2 weeks of grafting.

**Plan**
OT daily with PT; splint adjustment as edema changes; nursing to maintain elevation and splint position; teaching to Jenna.

title: Case Management Initial Assessment
author: T. Whitfield, RN CM
summary: CM assessment: commercial insurance through employer, home destroyed, partner as proxy, anticipated 3-4 week stay, rehab and burn clinic planning.
body:
**Reason**
Initial assessment for admission 11/2, 22% TBSA burn with inhalation injury, ICU.

**Insurance / Financial**
Employer-sponsored commercial PPO through the HVAC company; verification started with benefits office. Burn center in network; admission notification and concurrent review in progress. Not a workers' compensation case. Partner reports household income is primarily the patient's. Social work to assist with financial resources.

**Home Situation**
Lives with partner Jenna Whitaker and daughter Ava (6); house destroyed in the fire. Family currently staying with Jenna's mother. Red Cross/fire relief contact to be arranged by social work. Mother Linda Delaney arrived this afternoon.

**Decision-making**
Patient sedated. Full code. Jenna Whitaker at bedside, discussed as health care proxy; advance directive none.

**Anticipated Course**
ICU several days, excision and grafting planned this week. Expected total length of stay about 3-4 weeks (roughly 1 day per % TBSA) depending on grafting and wound healing.

**Discharge Planning Thoughts**
- Likely disposition: home with partner with home health versus acute rehab if hand function and mobility deficits remain. Needs a safe housing plan since the home was lost.
- Outpatient burn clinic follow-up, OT/PT for hand therapy, scar management, pressure garments, wound supplies and DME.
- Return to work: physical HVAC job requiring right-hand function; FMLA and short-term disability paperwork; employer contacted with family permission.
- Barriers: housing, transport, smoking cessation, alcohol counseling.

**Plan**
Follow daily; update team at interdisciplinary rounds; start FMLA paperwork; reassess once off ventilator.

title: Social Work and Chaplain Note
author: K. Abara, LCSW
summary: SW met partner Jenna Whitaker and mother Linda Delaney; daughter Ava safe with grandmother; guilt and distress, supports and ASAP counseling referral placed.
body:
**Reason**
Family support and psychosocial assessment, burn ICU day 1.

**Family**
Partner Jenna Whitaker at bedside; mother Linda Delaney arrived this afternoon. Daughter Ava, 6, uninjured, was checked in the ED and is staying with her maternal grandmother (Jenna's mother). No other children.

**Assessment**
- Jenna is tearful, anxious and sleep deprived, repeatedly saying she is relieved Ava is safe but frightened for Marcus. Expresses guilt that she did not wake him sooner and thoughts about what happened. She understands he is on a ventilator and has burns to the arm and chest. Ava has asked if her father is going to be okay and wants to see him; Jenna is unsure whether it is appropriate.
- Linda is supportive, coping with shock; will stay locally.
- Anticipate Marcus will have guilt and distress when awake given the circumstances.
- Substance use: alcohol use noted; no concerning pattern reported by partner, will screen after extubation.

**Child Safety**
Ava safe with grandmother, calm per Jenna; no concerns for her care identified, no child protective report indicated. Child life referral for preparation before a visit (burns, tubes and monitors).

**Supports / Resources**
Chaplain visit offered; Jenna accepted prayer support today. Provided waiting room, parking and meal vouchers. Red Cross assistance and fire relief resources shared (house lost). Burn survivor peer support information given.

**Referrals**
ASAP (Acute Stress and Adjustment Program) counseling referral placed for Jenna and Ava, and for Marcus once extubated.

**Plan**
SW follows daily during ICU stay, will attend family meeting with Dr. Okafor, assist with housing and financial applications with case management (T. Whitfield).
